sentences.text: This dinosaur reached a length of about 10 meters, stood 3.5 meters high at the hips, and weighed roughly 5 tons.
Its snout was rounded, a shape that differed from the square contours seen in other diplodocoids.
The neck bones possessed internal structures not found in any other known dinosaurs.
Two air pockets completely crossed the neural arches of the back vertebrae.
The species was first named in 2011 by a team of researchers including Fidel Torcida Fernández-Baldor and Leonardo Salgado.
Fossils were first collected between 2002 and 2004 by the Archaeological-Palaeontological Group of Salas de los Infantes.
Remains were recovered from the Tenadas de los Vallejos II site in the Sierra de la Demanda, Burgos Province, Spain.
The animal is classified within the family Rebbachisauridae.
It belongs to the parent group Rebbachisaurinae.
Demandasaurus is recognized as the only diagnosed rebbachisaurid species in Laurasia.
It was the first Diplodocoidean sauropod from the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago, described in Spain.
Demandasaurus lived approximately 129 to 123 million years ago during the early Cretaceous, between the Barremian and Aptian stages.
The dinosaur lived in what is now Europe.
